claim: Bicarbonate secretion is a fundamental process involved in maintaining acid-base homeostasis.
source: Bicarbonate secretion is a fundamental process involved in maintaining acid-base homeostasis.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about bicarbonate's role in physiology.

claim: Disruption of bicarbonate entry into airway lumen produces several defects in lung function due to thick mucus accumulation.
source: Disruption of bicarbonate entry into airway lumen, as has been observed in cystic fibrosis, produces several defects in lung function due to thick mucus accumulation.
evidence: This statement references observations in cystic fibrosis, drawing on established knowledge about CF pathophysiology.

claim: Bicarbonate is critical for correct mucin deployment.
source: Bicarbonate is critical for correct mucin deployment and there is increasing interest in understanding its role in airway physiology, particularly in the initiation of lung disease in children affected by cystic fibrosis, in the absence of detectable bacterial infection.
evidence: This is stated as an established fact in the field.

claim: CFTR and TMEM16A are apical anion exit channels in mammalian airways.
source: The current model of anion secretion in mammalian airways consists of CFTR and TMEM16A as apical anion exit channels, with limited capacity for bicarbonate transport compared to chloride.
evidence: This describes the current model in the field, representing established knowledge.

claim: CFTR and TMEM16A have limited capacity for bicarbonate transport compared to chloride.
source: The current model of anion secretion in mammalian airways consists of CFTR and TMEM16A as apical anion exit channels, with limited capacity for bicarbonate transport compared to chloride.
evidence: This is stated as part of the current understanding of these channels.

claim: CFTR and TMEM16A can couple to SLC26A4 anion exchanger to maximise bicarbonate secretion.
source: However, both channels can couple to SLC26A4 anion exchanger to maximise bicarbonate secretion.
evidence: This describes a known mechanism of bicarbonate secretion enhancement.

claim: Current models lack details about the identity of the basolateral protein(s) responsible for bicarbonate uptake into airway epithelial cells.
source: Nevertheless, current models lack any details about the identity of the basolateral protein(s) responsible for bicarbonate uptake into airway epithelial cells.
evidence: This identifies a gap in current knowledge that the study addresses.

claim: The electrogenic, sodium-dependent, bicarbonate cotransporter, SLC4A4, is expressed in the basolateral membrane of human and mouse airways.
source: We report herein that the electrogenic, sodium-dependent, bicarbonate cotransporter, SLC4A4, is expressed in the basolateral membrane of human and mouse airways, and that it's pharmacological inhibition or genetic silencing reduces bicarbonate secretion.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by immunolocalization data shown in Figure 2G,H and Figure 4B,C.

claim: Pharmacological inhibition or genetic silencing of SLC4A4 reduces bicarbonate secretion.
source: We report herein that the electrogenic, sodium-dependent, bicarbonate cotransporter, SLC4A4, is expressed in the basolateral membrane of human and mouse airways, and that it's pharmacological inhibition or genetic silencing reduces bicarbonate secretion.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from Ussing chamber experiments (Figure 1) and knockout mouse studies (Figure 4).

claim: SLC4A4 inhibition induced an acidification of the airways surface liquid in fully differentiated primary human airway cells cultures.
source: In fully differentiated primary human airway cells cultures, SLC4A4 inhibition induced an acidification of the airways surface liquid and markedly reduced the capacity of cells to recover from an acid load.
evidence: This is supported by ASL pH measurements shown in Figure 2A,B.

claim: SLC4A4 inhibition markedly reduced the capacity of cells to recover from an acid load.
source: In fully differentiated primary human airway cells cultures, SLC4A4 inhibition induced an acidification of the airways surface liquid and markedly reduced the capacity of cells to recover from an acid load.
evidence: This is supported by intracellular pH recovery experiments shown in Figure 1.

claim: Slc4a4-null mice have a previously unreported lung phenotype characterized by mucus accumulation and reduced mucociliary clearance.
source: Studies in the Slc4a4-null mice revealed a previously unreported lung phenotype, characterized by mucus accumulation and reduced mucociliary clearance.
evidence: This is supported by histological data (Figure 4D) and mucociliary clearance measurements (Figure 4H-J).

claim: Reduction of SLC4A4 function induced a CF-like phenotype even when chloride secretion remained intact.
source: Collectively, our results demonstrate that the reduction of SLC4A4 function induced a CF-like phenotype, even when chloride secretion remained intact, highlighting the important role SLC4A4 plays in bicarbonate secretion and mammalian airway function.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental results showing mucus accumulation and reduced MCC in Slc4a4-/- mice.

claim: Cystic fibrosis is the most common autosomal recessive disease in humans.
source: Even though, the pathophysiological consequences of decreased secretion of these anions has been extensively documented in cystic fibrosis (CF), the most common, autosomal recessive, disease in humans, there is still much discussion whether HCO3- secretion per se affects airway homeostasis (Zajac et al., 2021; Morrison et al., 2022).
evidence: This is established medical knowledge about CF.

claim: There is still much discussion whether HCO3- secretion per se affects airway homeostasis.
source: Even though, the pathophysiological consequences of decreased secretion of these anions has been extensively documented in cystic fibrosis (CF), the most common, autosomal recessive, disease in humans, there is still much discussion whether HCO3- secretion per se affects airway homeostasis (Zajac et al., 2021; Morrison et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citations to recent literature discussing this controversy.

claim: Impaired Cl- secretion reduces the volume of the airway surface liquid.
source: Impaired Cl- secretion reduces the volume of the fluid that covers the airway epithelium, the airway surface liquid (ASL), leading to ciliary dysfunction and promoting mucus stasis and airway obstruction (Cantin et al., 2006; Saint-Criq and Gray, 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Reduced ASL volume leads to ciliary dysfunction and promotes mucus stasis and airway obstruction.
source: Impaired Cl- secretion reduces the volume of the fluid that covers the airway epithelium, the airway surface liquid (ASL), leading to ciliary dysfunction and promoting mucus stasis and airway obstruction (Cantin et al., 2006; Saint-Criq and Gray, 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Deficient HCO3- secretion reduces ASL pH.
source: Deficient HCO3- secretion reduces ASL pH which compromises post-secretory mucin maturation and clearance (Hoegger et al., 2014), impairs the antimicrobial function of epithelial cells (Pezzulo et al., 2012; Shah et al., 2016) and increases fluid absorption, further decreasing ASL hydration (Garland et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Reduced ASL pH compromises post-secretory mucin maturation and clearance.
source: Deficient HCO3- secretion reduces ASL pH which compromises post-secretory mucin maturation and clearance (Hoegger et al., 2014), impairs the antimicrobial function of epithelial cells (Pezzulo et al., 2012; Shah et al., 2016) and increases fluid absorption, further decreasing ASL hydration (Garland et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Hoegger et al., 2014.

claim: Reduced ASL pH impairs the antimicrobial function of epithelial cells.
source: Deficient HCO3- secretion reduces ASL pH which compromises post-secretory mucin maturation and clearance (Hoegger et al., 2014), impairs the antimicrobial function of epithelial cells (Pezzulo et al., 2012; Shah et al., 2016) and increases fluid absorption, further decreasing ASL hydration (Garland et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Pezzulo et al., 2012 and Shah et al., 2016.

claim: Reduced ASL pH increases fluid absorption, further decreasing ASL hydration.
source: Deficient HCO3- secretion reduces ASL pH which compromises post-secretory mucin maturation and clearance (Hoegger et al., 2014), impairs the antimicrobial function of epithelial cells (Pezzulo et al., 2012; Shah et al., 2016) and increases fluid absorption, further decreasing ASL hydration (Garland et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Garland et al., 2013.

claim: Direct measurement of pH in the distal airways of CF children showed no acidification of the ASL.
source: Whilst direct measurement of pH in the distal airways of CF children showed no acidification of the ASL (Schultz et al., 2017), it has been demonstrated that the addition of HCO3- induced an increase in ASL height in human airway epithelial cells (hAECs) cultures and restored the normal properties of mucus from CF patients (Garland et al., 2013; Stigliani et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Schultz et al., 2017.

claim: Addition of HCO3- induced an increase in ASL height in human airway epithelial cells cultures.
source: Whilst direct measurement of pH in the distal airways of CF children showed no acidification of the ASL (Schultz et al., 2017), it has been demonstrated that the addition of HCO3- induced an increase in ASL height in human airway epithelial cells (hAECs) cultures and restored the normal properties of mucus from CF patients (Garland et al., 2013; Stigliani et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Garland et al., 2013 and Stigliani et al., 2016.

claim: Addition of HCO3- restored the normal properties of mucus from CF patients.
source: Whilst direct measurement of pH in the distal airways of CF children showed no acidification of the ASL (Schultz et al., 2017), it has been demonstrated that the addition of HCO3- induced an increase in ASL height in human airway epithelial cells (hAECs) cultures and restored the normal properties of mucus from CF patients (Garland et al., 2013; Stigliani et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Garland et al., 2013 and Stigliani et al., 2016.

claim: Aerosolized HCO3- into CF-pig airways increased bacterial killing.
source: Moreover, the use of aerosolized HCO3- into CF-pig airways increased bacterial killing, clearly indicating that HCO3- supplementation can correct inherent defects of CF in the airways (Pezzulo et al., 2012; Kim et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Pezzulo et al., 2012 and Kim et al., 2021.

claim: HCO3- is secreted by CFTR and TMEM16A channels in normal airways.
source: In normal airways, HCO3- is secreted by CFTR and TMEM16A channels, but after inflammatory signalling, HCO3- secretion is augmented through increased expression of the Cl- /HCO3- exchanger Pendrin (SLC26A4) (Han et al., 2016; Poulsen et al., 1994; Kim et al., 2019; Rehman et al., 2020; Garnett et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations describing the mechanisms of HCO3- secretion.

claim: After inflammatory signalling, HCO3- secretion is augmented through increased expression of Pendrin (SLC26A4).
source: In normal airways, HCO3- is secreted by CFTR and TMEM16A channels, but after inflammatory signalling, HCO3- secretion is augmented through increased expression of the Cl- /HCO3- exchanger Pendrin (SLC26A4) (Han et al., 2016; Poulsen et al., 1994; Kim et al., 2019; Rehman et al., 2020; Garnett et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations.

claim: The mechanism of basolateral HCO3- transport/uptake in native pulmonary tissues is still lacking.
source: Importantly, the mechanism of basolateral HCO3- transport/uptake in native pulmonary tissues is still lacking.
evidence: This identifies a knowledge gap that the study addresses.

claim: Primary hAECs express SLC4A4, SLC4A5, SLC4A7, and SLC4A8 at mRNA levels.
source: The use of specific primers (Supplementary file 1) for each NCBT revealed that SLC4A4, SLC4A5, SLC4A7, and SLC4A8 are expressed at mRNA levels in primary hAECs from three different individuals (P1, P2, P3, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A-E).
evidence: This is supported by PCR data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A-E.

claim: SLC4A10 showed near undetectable level of mRNA expression in primary hAECs.
source: SLC4A10 showed near undetectable level of mRNA expression (Figure 1—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This is supported by PCR data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1F.

claim: Isoforms B/C of NBCe1 were more highly expressed than isoform A in primary hAECs.
source: Interestingly, isoforms B/C of NBCe1 (known as the pancreatic isoform, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A) were more highly expressed than isoform A (known as the kidney isoform; Figure 1—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is supported by PCR data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A and 1E.

claim: SLC4A4 is the most expressed member of the SLC4A family in primary hAECs based on RNA-seq data.
source: Data extraction from previously published RNA-seq results (Saint-Criq et al., 2020) (GEO series accession number GSE154905) confirmed the pattern of expression of these isoforms (Figure 1—figure supplement 1G) and revealed that SLC4A4 is the most expressed member, closely followed by SLC4A7, SLC4A8, and SLC4A5.
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1G and cited from Saint-Criq et al., 2020.

claim: S0859 inhibited HCO3- secretion under unstimulated conditions in primary hAECs.
source: Results, shown in Figure 1 confirmed that, in the absence of stimulants, HCO3- secretion was inhibited by S0859 (Figure 1A and B) and that this pharmacological inhibitor did not have any effect on short-circuit current (Isc) in the absence of HCO3- (Figure 1D and E).
evidence: This is supported by Ussing chamber data shown in Figure 1A and B.

claim: S0859 did not have any effect on short-circuit current in the absence of HCO3- in primary hAECs.
source: Results, shown in Figure 1 confirmed that, in the absence of stimulants, HCO3- secretion was inhibited by S0859 (Figure 1A and B) and that this pharmacological inhibitor did not have any effect on short-circuit current (Isc) in the absence of HCO3- (Figure 1D and E).
evidence: This is supported by Ussing chamber data shown in Figure 1D and E.

claim: S0859 did not reduce Fsk-stimulated HCO3- secretion in primary hAECs under the tested conditions.
source: Interestingly, S0859 did not reduce Fsk-stimulated HCO3- secretion (Figure 1C) under these conditions.
evidence: This is supported by Ussing chamber data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: There is an electrogenic HCO3- transporter at the basolateral membrane of hAECs.
source: These results show that there is an electrogenic HCO3- transporter at the basolateral membrane of hAECs, which is consistent with SLC4A4, since SLC4A7 and SLC4A8 are electroneutral (Parker and Boron, 2013), and SLC4A5 has been shown to be localized to the apical membrane of renal epithelial cells and cholangiocytes (Gildea et al., 2015; Abuladze et al., 1998).
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data and cited literature about the properties of different SLC4A family members.

claim: SLC4A7 and SLC4A8 are electroneutral.
source: These results show that there is an electrogenic HCO3- transporter at the basolateral membrane of hAECs, which is consistent with SLC4A4, since SLC4A7 and SLC4A8 are electroneutral (Parker and Boron, 2013), and SLC4A5 has been shown to be localized to the apical membrane of renal epithelial cells and cholangiocytes (Gildea et al., 2015; Abuladze et al., 1998).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Parker and Boron, 2013.

claim: SLC4A5 has been shown to be localized to the apical membrane of renal epithelial cells and cholangiocytes.
source: These results show that there is an electrogenic HCO3- transporter at the basolateral membrane of hAECs, which is consistent with SLC4A4, since SLC4A7 and SLC4A8 are electroneutral (Parker and Boron, 2013), and SLC4A5 has been shown to be localized to the apical membrane of renal epithelial cells and cholangiocytes (Gildea et al., 2015; Abuladze et al., 1998).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Gildea et al., 2015 and Abuladze et al., 1998.

claim: Exposing cells bilaterally to a HCO3-/CO2-gassed KRB solution induced a transient acidification.
source: As shown in Figure 1E, exposing cells bilaterally to a HCO3-/CO2-gassed KRB solution induced a transient acidification.
evidence: This is supported by intracellular pH measurement data shown in Figure 1E (likely referring to Figure 1F based on the figure).

claim: Apical-only CO2 exposure in the absence of basolateral HCO3- induced a sustained acidification.
source: On the other hand, an apical-only CO2 exposure, in the absence of basolateral HCO3-, induced a sustained acidification (of the same amplitude as with bilateral HCO3-/CO2, Figure 1F and H), that recovered when HCO3- was re-introduced basolaterally (Figure 1F,I).
evidence: This is supported by intracellular pH measurement data shown in Figure 1F and H.

claim: pHi recovery from CO2-induced acidification depended on the presence of Na+ in the basolateral solution.
source: This pHi recovery depended on the presence of Na+ in the basolateral solution (Figure 1G) consistent with a Na+-coupled HCO3- transporter, which was confirmed using S0859 which blocked the pHi recovery from the CO2-induced acidification.
evidence: This is supported by intracellular pH measurement data shown in Figure 1G.

claim: S0859 blocked the pHi recovery from CO2-induced acidification.
source: This pHi recovery depended on the presence of Na+ in the basolateral solution (Figure 1G) consistent with a Na+-coupled HCO3- transporter, which was confirmed using S0859 which blocked the pHi recovery from the CO2-induced acidification.
evidence: This is supported by intracellular pH measurement data.

claim: S0859 significantly decreased the rate of pHi recovery from CO2-induced acidification in the presence of NHE inhibitor DMA.
source: In this condition, S0859 still significantly decreased the rate of pHi recovery from the CO2-induced acidification (Figure 1J and K).
evidence: This is supported by intracellular pH measurement data shown in Figure 1J and K (likely referring to Figure 1K and L based on the figure).

claim: NBCe1 inhibition significantly decreased ASL pH under resting conditions with a t1/2 of 46 min.
source: NBCe1 inhibition significantly decreased ASL pH under resting conditions with a t1/2 of 46 min (Figure 2A,B), and partially prevented the Fsk-induced increase in ASL pH which we have previously shown was via CFTR (Delpiano et al., 2018; Saint-Criq et al., 2019; Figure 2C,D), increasing the half-time response to Fsk from 25 to 31 min.
evidence: This is supported by ASL pH measurement data shown in Figure 2A,B.

claim: S0859 partially prevented the Fsk-induced increase in ASL pH.
source: NBCe1 inhibition significantly decreased ASL pH under resting conditions with a t1/2 of 46 min (Figure 2A,B), and partially prevented the Fsk-induced increase in ASL pH which we have previously shown was via CFTR (Delpiano et al., 2018; Saint-Criq et al., 2019; Figure 2C,D), increasing the half-time response to Fsk from 25 to 31 min.
evidence: This is supported by ASL pH measurement data shown in Figure 2C,D.

claim: Fsk-induced increase in ASL pH is via CFTR.
source: NBCe1 inhibition significantly decreased ASL pH under resting conditions with a t1/2 of 46 min (Figure 2A,B), and partially prevented the Fsk-induced increase in ASL pH which we have previously shown was via CFTR (Delpiano et al., 2018; Saint-Criq et al., 2019; Figure 2C,D), increasing the half-time response to Fsk from 25 to 31 min.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work by the authors (Delpiano et al., 2018; Saint-Criq et al., 2019).

claim: S0859 increased the half-time response to Fsk from 25 to 31 min.
source: NBCe1 inhibition significantly decreased ASL pH under resting conditions with a t1/2 of 46 min (Figure 2A,B), and partially prevented the Fsk-induced increase in ASL pH which we have previously shown was via CFTR (Delpiano et al., 2018; Saint-Criq et al., 2019; Figure 2C,D), increasing the half-time response to Fsk from 25 to 31 min.
evidence: This is supported by ASL pH measurement data shown in Figure 2C,D.

claim: When S0859 was added after Fsk, it significantly reduced the Fsk-induced, CFTR-dependent, increase in ASL pH with a half-time of 14 min.
source: Moreover, when S0859 was added after Fsk, it significantly reduced the Fsk-induced, CFTR-dependent, increase in ASL pH with a half-time of 14 min (Figure 2E,F) confirming the central role of SLC4A4 cotransporter in ASL pH homeostasis under both resting and stimulated conditions.
evidence: This is supported by ASL pH measurement data shown in Figure 2E,F.

claim: SLC4A4 locates in the basolateral membrane of acetylated tubulin positive human airway epithelial cells.
source: Finally, immunolocalization of SLC4A4 protein in human airway tissues showed intracellular and basolateral membrane staining in epithelial cells that were also positively stained for acetylated-tubulin indicating that SLC4A4 is preferentially expressed in ciliated cells in human airways (Figure 2G,H).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2G,H.

claim: SLC4A4 is preferentially expressed in ciliated cells in human airways.
source: Finally, immunolocalization of SLC4A4 protein in human airway tissues showed intracellular and basolateral membrane staining in epithelial cells that were also positively stained for acetylated-tubulin indicating that SLC4A4 is preferentially expressed in ciliated cells in human airways (Figure 2G,H).
evidence: This is an inference based on co-localization with acetylated-tubulin, a marker of ciliated cells, shown in Figure 2G,H.

claim: Several members of the SLC4 family including Slc4a4, Slc4a5, Slc4a7, and Slc4a10 are expressed in mouse airway epithelium.
source: To investigate the expression of SLC4 exchangers in mouse airway epithelium, we performed RT-PCR of epithelial cells from mouse tracheas and observed that several members of the SLC4 family including Slc4a4, Slc4a5, Slc4a7, and Slc4a10 were expressed (Figure 3—figure supplement 1 A-E).
evidence: This is supported by RT-PCR data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1 A-E.

claim: Slc4a4 isoform B/C but not isoform A is expressed in mouse airways.
source: Studies of Slc4a4 isoforms demonstrated that isoform B/C but not isoform A was expressed in mouse airways (Figure 3—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This is supported by RT-PCR data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1F.

claim: UTP-induced anion current was significantly reduced in the absence of HCO3- in mouse trachea.
source: Ussing chamber experiments performed in freshly excised mouse trachea using HCO3- (Figure 3A) or HEPES (Figure 3B) buffered solutions, showed that UTP-induced an anion current that was significantly reduced in the absence of HCO3- (–138±28 to -82±15 µA cm–2; p<0.01 Mann-Whitney test), but no significant effect on the cAMP-induced anion secretion, or the amiloride-sensitive sodium absorption (Figure 3C) was detected as previously shown (Anagnostopoulou et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by Ussing chamber data shown in Figure 3A-C.

claim: UTP had no significant effect on cAMP-induced anion secretion or amiloride-sensitive sodium absorption in mouse trachea.
source: Ussing chamber experiments performed in freshly excised mouse trachea using HCO3- (Figure 3A) or HEPES (Figure 3B) buffered solutions, showed that UTP-induced an anion current that was significantly reduced in the absence of HCO3- (–138±28 to -82±15 µA cm–2; p<0.01 Mann-Whitney test), but no significant effect on the cAMP-induced anion secretion, or the amiloride-sensitive sodium absorption (Figure 3C) was detected as previously shown (Anagnostopoulou et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by Ussing chamber data shown in Figure 3C and citation to Anagnostopoulou et al., 2012.

claim: Incubation of tracheas with acetazolamide didn't affect the magnitude of the UTP-induced current.
source: Complementary studies in HCO3- buffer showed that de novo synthesis of HCO3- was not participating in the UTP-induced electrogenic anion secretion, as incubation of tracheas with acetazolamide didn't affect the magnitude of the UTP-induced current (–124±14 µA cm–2; p>0.05 One-way ANOVA).
evidence: This is supported by Ussing chamber experiments with acetazolamide.

claim: De novo synthesis of HCO3- was not participating in the UTP-induced electrogenic anion secretion in mouse trachea.
source: Complementary studies in HCO3- buffer showed that de novo synthesis of HCO3- was not participating in the UTP-induced electrogenic anion secretion, as incubation of tracheas with acetazolamide didn't affect the magnitude of the UTP-induced current (–124±14 µA cm–2; p>0.05 One-way ANOVA).
evidence: This is an inference based on the lack of effect of acetazolamide, a carbonic anhydrase inhibitor.

claim: S0859 inhibited the cAMP-induced anion current in mouse trachea.
source: Using the SLC4A4 blocker S0859, we observed the inhibition of the cAMP-induced anion current (ΔIsc –12.2±2.4 µA cm–2) suggesting that SLC4A4 might participate in the cAMP-response (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A-C).
evidence: This is supported by Ussing chamber data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2A-C.

claim: Electrogenic-bicarbonate secretion was not significantly stimulated by cAMP in mouse trachea.
source: Nevertheless, when the TMEM16A/CFTR inhibitor, CaCCinhA01, was used to block the cAMP-induced current, further addition of S0859 was still able to induce a reduction in the current and of similar magnitude as shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2A (Figure 3—figure supplement 2D-F; –10.1±2.8 µA cm–2), confirming that electrogenic-bicarbonate secretion was not significantly stimulated by cAMP, indicating that basal HCO3- secretion occurs in mouse trachea.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that S0859 still had an effect after blocking cAMP-induced currents, shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2D-F.

claim: Basal HCO3- secretion occurs in mouse trachea.
source: Nevertheless, when the TMEM16A/CFTR inhibitor, CaCCinhA01, was used to block the cAMP-induced current, further addition of S0859 was still able to induce a reduction in the current and of similar magnitude as shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2A (Figure 3—figure supplement 2D-F; –10.1±2.8 µA cm–2), confirming that electrogenic-bicarbonate secretion was not significantly stimulated by cAMP, indicating that basal HCO3- secretion occurs in mouse trachea.
evidence: This is supported by Ussing chamber data showing S0859-sensitive current in the absence of stimulation (Figure 3D-F).

claim: S0859 reduced basal current only in HCO3- buffer in mouse trachea.
source: To confirm this last hypothesis we added S0589 to tissues pre-incubated with amiloride and observed a reduction in the basal current only in HCO3- buffer (–13.9±3.3 to -3.0±1.6 Δ µA cm–2 for HCO3- vs HEPES buffer; p<0.02; Mann-Whitney; Figure 3D–F).
evidence: This is supported by Ussing chamber data shown in Figure 3D-F.

claim: The UTP-induced anion secretion in tracheas maintained in HCO3- buffer was significantly reduced by previous addition of S0859.
source: As can be observed (Figure 3G and H) the UTP-induced anion secretion in tracheas maintained in HCO3- buffer was significantly reduced by previous addition of S0859 (–368±25 to -200±17 µA cm–2; p<0.001 One-way ANOVA).
evidence: This is supported by Ussing chamber data shown in Figure 3G and H.

claim: The UTP response was reduced when HCO3- was replaced with HEPES buffer in mouse trachea.
source: The UTP response was also reduced when HCO3- was replaced with HEPES buffer (Figure 3I) (–199±25 µA cm–2; p<0.001 One-way ANOVA), but the addition of S0859 induced no significant reduction of the UTP-induced anion secretion in tissues maintained in HEPES buffer (Figure 3J) (–142±12 µA cm–2; p>0.05 One-way ANOVA).
evidence: This is supported by Ussing chamber data shown in Figure 3I.

claim: Addition of S0859 induced no significant reduction of the UTP-induced anion secretion in tissues maintained in HEPES buffer.
source: The UTP response was also reduced when HCO3- was replaced with HEPES buffer (Figure 3I) (–199±25 µA cm–2; p<0.001 One-way ANOVA), but the addition of S0859 induced no significant reduction of the UTP-induced anion secretion in tissues maintained in HEPES buffer (Figure 3J) (–142±12 µA cm–2; p>0.05 One-way ANOVA).
evidence: This is supported by Ussing chamber data shown in Figure 3J.

claim: UTP induced an intracellular acidification in murine airway cells.
source: As shown in Figure 3L, UTP induced an intracellular acidification (ΔpHi –0.25±0.02) that was significantly reduced when cells were placed in low Cl- buffer (ΔpHi –0.11±0.02), indicating the existence of Cl-/HCO3- exchange.
evidence: This is supported by intracellular pH measurement data shown in Figure 3L.

claim: UTP-induced intracellular acidification was significantly reduced when cells were placed in low Cl- buffer, indicating the existence of Cl-/HCO3- exchange.
source: As shown in Figure 3L, UTP induced an intracellular acidification (ΔpHi –0.25±0.02) that was significantly reduced when cells were placed in low Cl- buffer (ΔpHi –0.11±0.02), indicating the existence of Cl-/HCO3- exchange.
evidence: This is an inference based on the reduced acidification in low Cl- conditions, shown in Figure 3L.

claim: UTP was almost unable to induce intracellular acidification in absence of HCO3-.
source: Figure 3M summarizes changes in intracellular pH and includes experiments in HEPES buffer, which shows that UTP was almost unable to induce intracellular acidification (ΔpHi –0.01±0.01) in absence of HCO3-.
evidence: This is supported by intracellular pH measurement data shown in Figure 3M.

claim: S0859 induced acidification of the intracellular compartment and prevented UTP-induced acidification in mouse airway cells.
source: To test if the UTP-induced intracellular acidification was dependent on SLC4A4 activity, we tested the S0859 inhibitor and observed acidification of the intracellular compartment and prevention of UTP-induced acidification (Figure 3—figure supplement 2G-H).
evidence: This is supported by intracellular pH measurement data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2G-H.

claim: Washout of S0859 partially restored pHi and UTP-induced acidification in mouse airway cells.
source: Washout of S0859 partially restored pHi and UTP-induced acidification. (Figure 3—figure supplement 2G-H; –0.05±0.01 to -0.13±0.03 ΔpHi, for UTP with S0559 and UTP post washout, respectively; p>0.002; Mann-Whitney).
evidence: This is supported by intracellular pH measurement data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2G-H.

claim: Both basal and UTP-induced HCO3- secretion are dependent on SLC4A4 activity in mouse airway epithelial cells.
source: These data suggest that both basal and UTP-induced HCO3- secretion are dependent on SLC4A4 activity in mouse airway epithelial cells.
evidence: This is an inference based on the effects of S0859 on basal and UTP-stimulated conditions.

claim: Slc4a4-/- animals were affected by defects in tracheal cartilage formation with the presence of ventral gaps and abnormal patterns on the rostrocaudal side.
source: First, we observed that Slc4a4-/- animals were affected by defects in tracheal cartilage formation with the presence of ventral gaps and abnormal patterns on the rostrocaudal side (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is supported by Alcian blue staining shown in Figure 4A.

claim: SLC4A4 signal was nearly absent in the airways from the Slc4a4-/- mice.
source: In wild-type animals, immunolocalization of SLC4A4 showed strong localization in the airway epithelium but the signal was nearly absent in the airways from the Slc4a4-/- mice (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: SLC4A4 was preferentially expressed in CCSP-positive cells (Club cells) in mouse airways.
source: Using the same antibody, we showed that SLC4A4 was preferentially expressed in CCSP-positive cells that correspond to Club cells and was excluded from cells positive to acetylated-Tubulin, that identify ciliated cells (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence co-localization data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: SLC4A4 was excluded from cells positive to acetylated-Tubulin (ciliated cells) in mouse airways.
source: Using the same antibody, we showed that SLC4A4 was preferentially expressed in CCSP-positive cells that correspond to Club cells and was excluded from cells positive to acetylated-Tubulin, that identify ciliated cells (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence co-localization data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Slc4a4-/- mouse airways demonstrated the presence of adherent mucus at the surface of the tracheal epithelium.
source: Further histological examination of the Slc4a4-/- mouse airways demonstrated the presence of adherent mucus at the surface of the tracheal epithelium (Figure 4D and Figure 4—figure supplement 1C,D) as well as in the bronchi (Figure 4—figure supplement 1E-G) and bronchioli (Figure 4—figure supplement 1H).
evidence: This is supported by histological data shown in Figure 4D and Figure 4—figure supplement 1C,D.

claim: Signs of damaged epithelium was observed as interruptions in the epithelial layer facing the lumen in the Slc4a4-/- airways.
source: Signs of damaged epithelium was also observed as interruptions in the epithelial layer facing the lumen in the Slc4a4-/- airways (Figure 4D and Figure 4—figure supplement 1F,H), that might explain the decreased Rte of the tracheas placed in Ussing chambers and that prevented electrophysiological measurements in the Slc4a4-/- tracheas (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is supported by histological data shown in Figure 4D and Figure 4—figure supplement 1F,H.

claim: Decreased Rte of the tracheas prevented electrophysiological measurements in the Slc4a4-/- tracheas.
source: Signs of damaged epithelium was also observed as interruptions in the epithelial layer facing the lumen in the Slc4a4-/- airways (Figure 4D and Figure 4—figure supplement 1F,H), that might explain the decreased Rte of the tracheas placed in Ussing chambers and that prevented electrophysiological measurements in the Slc4a4-/- tracheas (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is supported by Rte measurements shown in Figure 4E.

claim: A decrease in the magnitude of intracellular acidification was observed in Slc4a4-/- cells compared to wild type during UTP stimulation.
source: We observed a decrease in the magnitude of intracellular acidification in Slc4a4-/- cells when compared to those from wild type animals during UTP stimulation (–0.24±0.01 to -0.14±0.01 ΔpH[i], for wild type vs Slc4a4-/-) suggesting that an important amount of HCO3- accumulates in airways cells via SLC4A4 (Figure 4F–G).
evidence: This is supported by intracellular pH measurement data shown in Figure 4F-G.

claim: An important amount of HCO3- accumulates in airways cells via SLC4A4.
source: We observed a decrease in the magnitude of intracellular acidification in Slc4a4-/- cells when compared to those from wild type animals during UTP stimulation (–0.24±0.01 to -0.14±0.01 ΔpH[i], for wild type vs Slc4a4-/-) suggesting that an important amount of HCO3- accumulates in airways cells via SLC4A4 (Figure 4F–G).
evidence: This is an inference based on the reduced acidification in Slc4a4-/- cells.

claim: After UTP wash-out, the acidification persisted in the wild type cells but not in the Slc4a4-/-.
source: We also noticed that after UTP wash-out, the acidification persisted in the wild type cells but not in the Slc4a4-/- (Figure 4—figure supplement 1J; –0.09±0.02 to -0.02±0.01 ΔpH[i], for wild type vs Slc4a4-/-), suggesting that HCO3- secretion was sustained by SLC4A4 activity.
evidence: This is supported by intracellular pH measurement data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1J.

claim: HCO3- secretion was sustained by SLC4A4 activity.
source: We also noticed that after UTP wash-out, the acidification persisted in the wild type cells but not in the Slc4a4-/- (Figure 4—figure supplement 1J; –0.09±0.02 to -0.02±0.01 ΔpH[i], for wild type vs Slc4a4-/-), suggesting that HCO3- secretion was sustained by SLC4A4 activity.
evidence: This is an inference based on the difference in post-UTP acidification between wild type and Slc4a4-/- cells.

claim: Plastic beads covered a larger distance in wild type tissues compared to Slc4a4-/- trachea.
source: As shown in the polar plots in Figure 4H the plastic beads covered a larger distance in wild type tissues and, in some cases, retrograde movement of beads was observed in the Slc4a4-/- trachea.
evidence: This is supported by mucociliary clearance data shown in Figure 4H.

claim: Retrograde movement of beads was observed in the Slc4a4-/- trachea.
source: As shown in the polar plots in Figure 4H the plastic beads covered a larger distance in wild type tissues and, in some cases, retrograde movement of beads was observed in the Slc4a4-/- trachea.
evidence: This is supported by mucociliary clearance data shown in Figure 4H.

claim: A similar reduction in distance travelled was observed in wild type tissues bathed in HEPES buffer.
source: A similar reduction in distance travelled was observed in wild type tissues bathed in HEPES buffer.
evidence: This is supported by mucociliary clearance data.

claim: The use of HEPES buffer in the Slc4a4-/- tracheas showed no further effect on both speed and total distance travelled by the beads.
source: The use of HEPES buffer in the Slc4a4-/- tracheas showed no further effect on both speed and total distance travelled by the beads.
evidence: This is supported by mucociliary clearance data shown in Figure 4I and J.

claim: Mucociliary clearance is significantly decreased when HCO3- transport is impaired after Slc4a4 silencing.
source: This data set demonstrates that mucociliary clearance is significantly decreased when HCO3- transport is impaired after Slc4a4 silencing.
evidence: This is an inference based on the mucociliary clearance data from Slc4a4-/- mice.

claim: The specificity of S0859 for SLC4A4 is uncertain.
source: As the specificity of S0859 for SLC4A4 has been discussed and is still unclear (Heidtmann et al., 2015; Schwab et al., 2005; Ch'en et al., 2008), it is uncertain from our data whether SLC4A4 is the main and only actor regulating bicarbonate uptake in primary hAECs.
evidence: This is supported by citations discussing the specificity of S0859.

claim: The importance of SLC4A4 in airway pH homeostasis is supported by strong evidence from the use of knock-out animals.
source: However its importance in airway pH homeostasis is supported by strong evidence from the use of knock-out animals.
evidence: This refers to the data from Slc4a4-/- mice presented in the study.

claim: Early characterization in canine and human airway epithelium indicated that HCO3- secretion occurs via CFTR, is activated by cAMP and dependent on basolateral Na+.
source: Early characterization in canine and human airway epithelium indicated that HCO3- secretion occurs via CFTR, is activated by cAMP and dependent on basolateral Na+ Smith and Welsh, 1992, similar features were observed in the Calu-3 cell line (Devor et al., 1999).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Smith and Welsh, 1992 and Devor et al., 1999.

claim: HCO3- secretion in the mouse airways is mostly Ca+2- rather than cAMP-activated.
source: Nevertheless, and in contrast to human airway epithelium, our present data shows that HCO3- secretion in the mouse airways is mostly Ca+2- rather than cAMP-activated, but both human and mouse share a basal secretory component for HCO3- previously observed in human bronchioles (Shamsuddin and Quinton, 2019), and that we now show is dependent on SLC4A4 activity.
evidence: This is supported by the Ussing chamber data showing UTP (Ca2+) responses in mouse trachea.

claim: Both human and mouse share a basal secretory component for HCO3-.
source: Nevertheless, and in contrast to human airway epithelium, our present data shows that HCO3- secretion in the mouse airways is mostly Ca+2- rather than cAMP-activated, but both human and mouse share a basal secretory component for HCO3- previously observed in human bronchioles (Shamsuddin and Quinton, 2019), and that we now show is dependent on SLC4A4 activity.
evidence: This is supported by the current study's data and citation to Shamsuddin and Quinton, 2019.

claim: Basolateral localization of SLC4A4 was previously demonstrated in the Calu-3 cell line.
source: Basolateral localization of SLC4A4 was previously demonstrated in the Calu-3 cell line (Kreindler et al., 2006) but up to the date there has been no other studies investigating SLC4A4 localization in native airway tissues.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Kreindler et al., 2006.

claim: The sole expression of SLC4A4 does not assure HCO3- secretion as apical CFTR is also necessary.
source: Nevertheless, it must be considered that the sole expression of SLC4A4 does not assure HCO3- secretion as compelling evidence has demonstrated that apical CFTR is also necessary.
evidence: This is an inference based on established knowledge about the requirement for both basolateral uptake and apical exit mechanisms.

claim: The calcium-activated TMEM16A channel has been shown to be expressed in goblet cells.
source: While the calcium-activated TMEM16A channel has been shown to be expressed in goblet cells (Scudieri et al., 2012), both HCO3- transporters, CFTR and pendrin, have been localized in the apical membrane of ciliated hAECs cells supporting our observation (Kim et al., 2019; Kreda et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Scudieri et al., 2012.

claim: CFTR and pendrin have been localized in the apical membrane of ciliated hAECs cells.
source: While the calcium-activated TMEM16A channel has been shown to be expressed in goblet cells (Scudieri et al., 2012), both HCO3- transporters, CFTR and pendrin, have been localized in the apical membrane of ciliated hAECs cells supporting our observation (Kim et al., 2019; Kreda et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Kim et al., 2019 and Kreda et al., 2005.

claim: SLC4A4-B, and not isoform A, is functionally coupled to CFTR through the IRBIT protein in pancreatic ducts.
source: Moreover, it has been demonstrated that SLC4A4-B, that we detected in human and mouse, and not the isoform A, is functionally coupled to CFTR through the IRBIT protein in pancreatic ducts (Yang et al., 2009; Shirakabe et al., 2006), further supporting the idea that a functional coupling in the same cell type is necessary for efficient HCO3- secretion.
evidence: This is supported by citations to Yang et al., 2009 and Shirakabe et al., 2006.

claim: CFTR and Pendrin expression increases in secretory cells after cytokine stimulation, but SLC4A4 remained unaltered.
source: Even though, CFTR and Pendrin expression increases in secretory cells after cytokine stimulation, SLC4A4 remained unaltered, suggesting that other basolateral HCO3- transporter support HCO3- secretion in human secretory cells during the inflammatory response (Rehman et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Rehman et al., 2020.

claim: The pulmonary ionocyte is a rare airway epithelial cell type that contains the highest amount of CFTR/Cftr transcripts in human and mouse.
source: Finally, CFTR distribution in airway epithelium has been under renewed scrutiny after the recent discovery of the pulmonary ionocyte, a rare airway epithelial cell type that contains the highest amount of CFTR/Cftr transcripts in human and mouse (Montoro et al., 2018; Plasschaert et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Montoro et al., 2018 and Plasschaert et al., 2018.

claim: Most human airway epithelial cell types express CFTR including ciliated cells.
source: Nevertheless, recent and detailed studies demonstrate that most human airway epithelial cell types express CFTR including ciliated cells as was initially demonstrated (Engelhardt et al., 1994; Okuda et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Engelhardt et al., 1994 and Okuda et al., 2021.

claim: SLC4A4 localization in mouse was different from human airway epithelium, as the mouse SLC4A4 was expressed in CCSP+ and not ciliated cells.
source: We noticed that SLC4A4 localization in mouse was different from human airway epithelium, as the mouse SLC4A4 was expressed in CCSP +and not ciliated cells.
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: CFTR and TMEM16A channels were specifically located in non-ciliated cells of mouse airways.
source: Previously, CFTR and TMEM16A channels were specifically located in non-ciliated cells of mouse airways (Hahn et al., 2018), a distribution also conserved in the rat (Hahn et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Hahn et al., 2018 and Hahn et al., 2017.

claim: Pendrin was detected in non-ciliated secretory MUC5AC+ cells in mouse airways.
source: Pendrin, was also detected in non-ciliated secretory MUC5AC + cells, suggesting that a functional coupling for HCO3- secretion occurs in secretory non-ciliated cells of the mouse airways (Jia et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Jia et al., 2016.

claim: A functional coupling for HCO3- secretion occurs in secretory non-ciliated cells of the mouse airways.
source: Pendrin, was also detected in non-ciliated secretory MUC5AC + cells, suggesting that a functional coupling for HCO3- secretion occurs in secretory non-ciliated cells of the mouse airways (Jia et al., 2016).
evidence: This is an inference based on the co-localization of transporters in the same cell type.

claim: CFTR is not the principal Cl- transporter in the mouse airways.
source: Such a difference in expression of transporter proteins among human and mouse airways has frequently been described; for example CFTR, is not the principal Cl- transporter in the mouse airways and consequently silencing or mutation of Cftr in mice did not produce CF disease of the lungs (Ratcliff et al., 1993; Snouwaert et al., 1992).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Ratcliff et al., 1993 and Snouwaert et al., 1992.

claim: Silencing or mutation of Cftr in mice did not produce CF disease of the lungs.
source: Such a difference in expression of transporter proteins among human and mouse airways has frequently been described; for example CFTR, is not the principal Cl- transporter in the mouse airways and consequently silencing or mutation of Cftr in mice did not produce CF disease of the lungs (Ratcliff et al., 1993; Snouwaert et al., 1992).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Ratcliff et al., 1993 and Snouwaert et al., 1992.

claim: The ATP12A H+/K+ ATPase is expressed in human and not mouse airways.
source: Furthermore, the expression in human and not mouse airways of another protein that influence ASL pH, the ATP12A H+/K+ ATPase, magnifies ASL acidification in human airways in CF disease (Shah et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Shah et al., 2016.

claim: The silencing of Slc4a4 induced a muco-obstructive phenotype in the mouse.
source: As observed here, the silencing of Slcl4a4 induced a muco-obstructive phenotype in the mouse, whereas the silencing of Slc12a2, which encodes the bumetanide-sensitive NKCC1 co-transporter, which is essential for Cl- accumulation and secretion, did not (Grubb et al., 2001), suggesting that lack of HCO3- is pathologically more relevant than Cl- secretion in mouse airways.
evidence: This is supported by the histological and functional data from Slc4a4-/- mice and citation to Grubb et al., 2001.

claim: The silencing of Slc12a2 did not produce a muco-obstructive phenotype in the mouse.
source: As observed here, the silencing of Slcl4a4 induced a muco-obstructive phenotype in the mouse, whereas the silencing of Slc12a2, which encodes the bumetanide-sensitive NKCC1 co-transporter, which is essential for Cl- accumulation and secretion, did not (Grubb et al., 2001), suggesting that lack of HCO3- is pathologically more relevant than Cl- secretion in mouse airways.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Grubb et al., 2001.

claim: Lack of HCO3- is pathologically more relevant than Cl- secretion in mouse airways.
source: As observed here, the silencing of Slcl4a4 induced a muco-obstructive phenotype in the mouse, whereas the silencing of Slc12a2, which encodes the bumetanide-sensitive NKCC1 co-transporter, which is essential for Cl- accumulation and secretion, did not (Grubb et al., 2001), suggesting that lack of HCO3- is pathologically more relevant than Cl- secretion in mouse airways.
evidence: This is an inference based on the comparison of phenotypes between Slc4a4-/- and Slc12a2-/- mice.

claim: hAEC from CF patients produce acidic ASL and mucus that is more viscous than in cells from non-CF donors.
source: For example, hAEC from CF patients produce acidic ASL and mucus that is more viscous than in cells from non-CF donors (Tang et al., 2016), the acidification of the ASL induced abnormal epithelial immune responses and reduced MCC that could be reversed after HCO3- supplementation (Pezzulo et al., 2012; Shah et al., 2016; Ferrera et al., 2021; Simonin et al., 2019; Birket et al., 2018; Cooper et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Tang et al., 2016.

claim: The acidification of the ASL induced abnormal epithelial immune responses and reduced MCC that could be reversed after HCO3- supplementation.
source: For example, hAEC from CF patients produce acidic ASL and mucus that is more viscous than in cells from non-CF donors (Tang et al., 2016), the acidification of the ASL induced abnormal epithelial immune responses and reduced MCC that could be reversed after HCO3- supplementation (Pezzulo et al., 2012; Shah et al., 2016; Ferrera et al., 2021; Simonin et al., 2019; Birket et al., 2018; Cooper et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations.

claim: HCO3- secretion is necessary for proper mucus release from hAECs.
source: Furthermore, HCO3- secretion is necessary for proper mucus release from hAECs (Gorrieri et al., 2016), and maintenance of normal amounts of ENaC-mediated Na+ absorption and ASL volume (Garland et al., 2013), functions that become abnormal due to acidic ASL pH.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Gorrieri et al., 2016.

claim: HCO3- secretion is necessary for maintenance of normal amounts of ENaC-mediated Na+ absorption and ASL volume.
source: Furthermore, HCO3- secretion is necessary for proper mucus release from hAECs (Gorrieri et al., 2016), and maintenance of normal amounts of ENaC-mediated Na+ absorption and ASL volume (Garland et al., 2013), functions that become abnormal due to acidic ASL pH.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Garland et al., 2013.

claim: The reduction of HCO3- transport after SLC4A4 inhibition is consistent with the expected muco-obstructive phenotype, including reduced MCC and mucus accumulation.
source: Even though technically challenging issues prevented us from measuring ASL pH in the mouse trachea, the reduction of HCO3- transport demonstrated here after SLC4A4 inhibition is consistent with the expected muco-obstructive phenotype, including reduced MCC and mucus accumulation.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data from Slc4a4-/- mice.

claim: The Slc4a4-null animal and the Slc4a4W516X/W516X avatar mouse are affected by severe metabolic acidosis due to proximal renal tubular acidosis.
source: The Slc4a4-null animal, corresponding to the one used in the present studies, and the Slc4a4W516X/W516X avatar mouse engineered to mimic a non-sense mutation found in a human patient, are affected by severe metabolic acidosis due to proximal renal tubular acidosis (pRTA; Gawenis et al., 2007; Lo et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Gawenis et al., 2007 and Lo et al., 2011.

claim: Decreased plasma HCO3- is observed in the Slc4a4-/- mice.
source: Even though, decreased plasma HCO3- is observed in the Slc4a4-/- mice (5.3±0.5 mM; Gawenis et al., 2007), is unlikely that reduced HCO3- availability influenced mucus accumulation in the airways, as we have previously determined that the transporter is fully saturated at 3 mM HCO3- (Theparambil et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Gawenis et al., 2007.

claim: It is unlikely that reduced HCO3- availability influenced mucus accumulation in the airways, as the transporter is fully saturated at 3 mM HCO3-.
source: Even though, decreased plasma HCO3- is observed in the Slc4a4-/- mice (5.3±0.5 mM; Gawenis et al., 2007), is unlikely that reduced HCO3- availability influenced mucus accumulation in the airways, as we have previously determined that the transporter is fully saturated at 3 mM HCO3- (Theparambil et al., 2014).
evidence: This is an inference based on previous work cited (Theparambil et al., 2014) showing transporter saturation.

claim: Extra-renal manifestations of Slc4a4 silencing in the mouse include growth retardation, ocular band keratopathy, splenomegaly, abnormal dentition and intestinal obstructions.
source: Extra-renal manifestations of Slc4a4 silencing in the mouse include growth retardation, ocular band keratopathy, splenomegaly, abnormal dentition and intestinal obstructions, most of which mimics the clinical findings observed in human patients.
evidence: This is stated as known information about Slc4a4-/- mice.

claim: Lung defects have not been reported in human patients with SLC4A4 mutations.
source: Nevertheless lung defects have not been reported in human patients, and observation which could be explained by the fact that human disease is milder than in mouse models.
evidence: This is stated as an observation about human patients.

claim: Human disease is milder than in mouse models of Slc4a4 deficiency.
source: Nevertheless lung defects have not been reported in human patients, and observation which could be explained by the fact that human disease is milder than in mouse models.
evidence: This is speculation to explain the difference between human and mouse phenotypes.

claim: At birth human kidneys are functionally more mature than in mouse.
source: This might be related to the fact that at birth human kidneys are functionally more mature than in mouse (Takahashi et al., 2000) and for example, while heterozygous animals present mild pRTA, human patients bearing heterozygous SLC4A4 mutations did not show any signs of disease (Gawenis et al., 2007; Lo et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Takahashi et al., 2000.

claim: Heterozygous Slc4a4 animals present mild pRTA.
source: This might be related to the fact that at birth human kidneys are functionally more mature than in mouse (Takahashi et al., 2000) and for example, while heterozygous animals present mild pRTA, human patients bearing heterozygous SLC4A4 mutations did not show any signs of disease (Gawenis et al., 2007; Lo et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Gawenis et al., 2007 and Lo et al., 2011.

claim: Human patients bearing heterozygous SLC4A4 mutations did not show any signs of disease.
source: This might be related to the fact that at birth human kidneys are functionally more mature than in mouse (Takahashi et al., 2000) and for example, while heterozygous animals present mild pRTA, human patients bearing heterozygous SLC4A4 mutations did not show any signs of disease (Gawenis et al., 2007; Lo et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Gawenis et al., 2007 and Lo et al., 2011.

claim: Compensatory activity of other Na+-coupled HCO3- cotransporters or exchangers has been discarded in mouse.
source: Even though, a compensatory activity of other Na+-coupled HCO3- cotransporters, or exchangers, has been discarded in mouse, this possibility has not been examined in humans where compensatory activity might benefit patient's health (Lo et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Lo et al., 2011.

claim: The possibility of compensatory activity has not been examined in humans where compensatory activity might benefit patient's health.
source: Even though, a compensatory activity of other Na+-coupled HCO3- cotransporters, or exchangers, has been discarded in mouse, this possibility has not been examined in humans where compensatory activity might benefit patient's health (Lo et al., 2011).
evidence: This is speculation about potential compensatory mechanisms in humans.

claim: Both the Slc4a4-/- and W516X-mutant animals die soon after weaning.
source: Both the Slc4a4-/- and W516X-mutant animals die soon after weaning as we also observed, but while the specific knock-out mouse for SLC4A4 isoform A (NBCe1-A) has a normal life span, the knock-out mouse for SLC4A4 isoforms B and C (NBCe1-B/C) is still lethal.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the current study and known information about these mouse models.

claim: The specific knock-out mouse for SLC4A4 isoform A (NBCe1-A) has a normal life span.
source: Both the Slc4a4-/- and W516X-mutant animals die soon after weaning as we also observed, but while the specific knock-out mouse for SLC4A4 isoform A (NBCe1-A) has a normal life span, the knock-out mouse for SLC4A4 isoforms B and C (NBCe1-B/C) is still lethal.
evidence: This is stated as known information about these mouse models.

claim: The knock-out mouse for SLC4A4 isoforms B and C (NBCe1-B/C) is still lethal.
source: Both the Slc4a4-/- and W516X-mutant animals die soon after weaning as we also observed, but while the specific knock-out mouse for SLC4A4 isoform A (NBCe1-A) has a normal life span, the knock-out mouse for SLC4A4 isoforms B and C (NBCe1-B/C) is still lethal.
evidence: This is stated as known information about these mouse models.

claim: The cause of death of the Slc4a4-/- animals was not due to metabolic acidosis, but rather due to extra renal phenotypes worsened by pRTA.
source: This suggests that the cause of death of the animals was not due to metabolic acidosis, but rather due to extra renal phenotypes worsened by pRTA (Salerno et al., 2019; Lee et al., 2018).
evidence: This is an inference supported by citations to Salerno et al., 2019 and Lee et al., 2018.

claim: Lethality of Slc4a4-/- mice is dependent on the genetic background of the animals.
source: This observation might also be linked to the influence of modifier genes as observed in human patients and CF mouse models (Rozmahel et al., 1996; Cutting, 2010; Philp et al., 2018). In this regard, our observation that lethality is dependent on the genetic background of the animals supports such a possibility.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A-B and citations about modifier genes.
